topics.label: Introduction and lecture framing
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture as an integration of previously introduced immune cells and molecules.

topics.label: Principles of innate recognition through PAMPs, DAMPs and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how innate immune receptors distinguish signs of infection or damage from normal host components.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor recognition and signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how Toll-like receptors translate microbial recognition into immune responses shaped by the location of receptor activation.

topics.label: Non-TLR recognition and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how recognition pathways beyond Toll-like receptors activate inflammation and can contribute to inflammatory disease.

topics.label: Sentinel-cell activation and recruitment of inflammatory cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics follow how activated sentinel cells mobilise inflammation, developing the recruitment signal into the mechanisms that bring leukocytes to an infection.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how dendritic cells carry evidence of tissue infection through lymphatic drainage to initiate adaptive responses in lymph nodes.

topics.label: Excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how excessive inflammatory activation becomes a systemic, life-threatening process.

topics.label: Passive and active resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammation subsides through withdrawal of activating stimuli and the increasing influence of inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine why inflamed tissue may fail to return to normal, including how persistent inflammation can contain an infection that cannot be cleared.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture on complement
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the lecture and announces the subject of the next session.
